previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and chronic diarrhea, was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea following a home flood. He was found to have acute kidney injury due to hypovolemia and urinary retention. A catheter was placed, and IV fluids were given, leading to improvement in renal function by hospital day 2. His nausea persisted, but infectious workup was negative, and he gradually tolerated oral intake. Tube feeds were restarted and advanced. He refused a planned flexible sigmoidoscopy but was able to maintain nutrition. He passed a void trial and was discharged home with stable kidney function, instructions to resume tube feeds, and recommendations for urology and PCP follow-up, including electrolyte monitoring due to prolonged QT syndrome.
